equity_bridge.item: Restoration and rehabilitation provisions, after tax at 27%
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 balance sheet note D.5: A$24.9m current + A$313.9m non-current = A$338.8m, less a 27% tax shield on the eventual spend. Covers Lynas Malaysia residue storage, Kalgoorlie and Mt Weld. Not in EBITDA, so charged here once.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR from the volume x price build; no historical CAGR is a usable anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (17.3% 3yr, 26.4% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (9.8%, 14.9%) and EPS (-13.3%, 4.2%). Equity growth is mostly issuance: A$425m raised in FY2021, A$214m in FY2023 and A$933m in FY2026. It is not a measure of compounding and was rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = operating cash flow - capex - SBC; interest received sits in investing activities in every year, so no interest strip is needed. Owner FCF: FY2021 A$172.2m, FY2022 A$269.4m, FY2023 -A$216.0m, FY2024 -A$551.5m, FY2025 -A$333.8m, FY2026 A$126.3m. The 3-year FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2023 was negative (A$1.6bn of capex across FY2023-FY2025 for Kalgoorlie, the Mt Weld expansion and Lynas Malaysia). Every endpoint is a different point in the NdPr price cycle (average selling price A$29.8/kg in FY2021, A$60.3 in FY2022, A$38.1 in FY2024, A$80.7 in FY2026), so these CAGRs describe the cycle more than the business.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle. The Mt Weld, Kalgoorlie and Lynas Malaysia investments reach roughly 10,000tpa of NdPr by FY2030, short of the 12ktpa stretch target. The JARE floor of US$110/kg holds on its 5,000tpa of firm offtake through 2038, while the other half of volume sells at a market price that eases from about US$100/kg today to about US$80/kg as Chinese supply policy normalises. Heavy rare earths (Dy, Tb, Sm, then Gd and Y from FY2028) add a modest stream. EBITDA margin settles at 46%, above the 42% six-year average because half the book is now floor-priced, and capex falls to depreciation once the A$294m heavy rare earths expansion is finished.
scenario_narratives.bull: Western governments keep paying for ex-China supply. The market NdPr price stays at or above the floor on all volume, Lynas fills the full 12ktpa, the upside-sharing arrangement above US$150/kg comes into play in some years, and separated heavy rare earths sell at ex-China prices well above the China index. Downstream ties to JS Link, Noveon and LS Eco Energy lock in demand. Fixed-cost absorption takes the EBITDA margin to about 60%, close to the 65% seen in FY2022, and the new permanent CEO executes the Malaysian residue-process change without disruption.
scenario_narratives.bear: China loosens export controls or lifts quotas and the market NdPr price drops back to the US$55-60/kg seen in mid-2025. The floor covers only the firm JARE tonnage, and the clause that volumes and prices are agreed between Lynas, JARE and each customer proves softer than the headline. The ramp-up problems of FY2026 (Mt Weld ore variation, water recycling, Kalgoorlie power) persist and volume stalls near 8,500tpa on a cost base built for 12ktpa. The 2031 deadline to stop producing radioactive WLP residue in Malaysia needs an unproven industrial process and adds capex, so capex stays above depreciation and the margin sits at 32%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Lynas is valued as a cyclical processor at mid-cycle, not on FY2026 or the current spot price. The value comes from three things: how many tonnes of NdPr the new plants actually deliver, what the half of the book not covered by the US$110/kg floor sells for, and how much capex the business needs once the build-out ends. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF, the low end of the house range for cyclicals. Net cash of A$870.7m, most of it raised in FY2026 for the Towards 2030 growth plan, is counted at face value; the returns on spending it are not.
key_risks_to_valuation: NdPr market price: roughly half of volume is uncovered, and each US$10/kg on that half moves revenue by about A$75m a year at 10,000tpa
Durability and enforceability of the JARE US$110/kg floor through 2038, and of the smaller US Government agreement
Volume: the base case assumes 10,000tpa NdPr against 7,260t produced in FY2026 and a history of ramp-up slippage
Malaysian licence condition requiring an end to WLP residue above 1 Bq/g by March 2031, using a process not yet proven at industrial scale
Capex overruns: the heavy rare earths expansion budget has already risen from about A$180m to about A$294m
AUD/USD: sales are in USD and most costs in AUD and MYR; the build assumes roughly 0.65
Deployment of the A$1.2bn cash balance into downstream and resource projects whose returns are not modelled
The terminal value cap binds in the base and bull cases; a buyer paying a strategic premium for ex-China supply would justify more than 12x

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 10.69-22.37
data_sources.financials: LYC.AX_Metrics.csv (FY2015-FY2026) and the FY2026 annual report: statement of financial position, cash flow statement, notes A.2 (finance income and costs), A.4 (tax), B.2 (leases), C.3 (borrowings), D.5 (provisions), and the Directors' Report operating review
data_sources.qualitative: LYC.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), including the September-quarter FY2027 figures, which are not in the extracted filings

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,006.503m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 plus 4.046m performance rights (FY2026 annual report, Directors' Report). Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The FY2026 placement and SPP (70.4m shares, A$932.6m gross) is already in both the count and the cash.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income was A$38.5m in FY2026 (A$32.2m received in cash) and net cash is material, but Lynas classifies interest received in INVESTING activities, so it is not inside operating cash flow or reported FCF. Nothing is deducted because nothing is there to strip; deducting it would charge it twice. The forward build starts from EBITDA, which also excludes it.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report cash-flow reconciliation, 'Share-based payments 14,278' (A$'000); equity-settled performance rights, no cash tax on net settlement disclosed
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% in AUD, the flows' own currency: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% plus ~6% equity risk premium at a beta near 1.0. The balance sheet is net cash, so WACC is effectively cost of equity. No extra premium is added for commodity cyclicality, China price-setting or the Malaysian licence condition, and the rate is the same in all three scenarios: those risks are carried in the scenario flows and weights, and charging them again in the rate would count them twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Lease liabilities of A$218.7m (A$5.0m current + A$213.7m non-current, almost all the Zenith Energy power-purchase agreement for the Mt Weld hybrid power station) are inside total_debt. Lease payments (A$20.6m principal in financing, A$15.0m lease interest expense in FY2026) are NOT deducted from the flows, and lease_cost_pct_path is zero. EBITDA margins are therefore the reported post-AASB 16 basis.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests; all profit is attributable to equity holders of the parent.
inputs.net_debt_composition: Cash and cash equivalents A$504.1m plus short-term deposits A$705.0m = A$1,209.1m. Debt: JARE loan A$119.7m (A$27.7m current + A$92.0m non-current) plus lease liabilities A$218.7m = A$338.4m. Net cash A$870.7m.
inputs.subsequent_events_note: After balance date (July 2026) Lynas invested ~A$50m in JS Link ordinary equity and agreed a ~A$29m cross-subscription of convertible instruments with LS Eco Energy. These convert cash into investments carried at cost, so they are value-neutral here and net cash is left at the 30 June 2026 figure. The September-quarter balance sheet is not in the research folder; refresh net cash when the H1 FY2027 report lands.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Lynas is an operating miner and processor whose value is a stream of free cash flow; it is not a developer, so no NAV/NPV route. MID-CYCLE FRAMING: FY2026 (revenue A$977.9m, EBITDA A$386.0m, NPAT A$222.4m) is neither a trough nor a normal year, so no scenario carries the FY2026 margin forward. Each scenario is a volume x price view: NdPr volume ramps from 7,337t sold in FY2026 toward the 10.5-12ktpa capacity the Lynas 2025 investments were built for, and price is split between the ~5,000tpa under the JARE US$110/kg NdPr floor and the remainder at a scenario-specific market price. The China domestic NdPr price has ranged from roughly US$40/kg to above US$140/kg since 2019 and was US$55.0/kg in June 2025 and US$100.8/kg in June 2026. FLAT COUNT: Lynas does not buy back shares; performance rights are settled with new shares, so the flat count is a modelling convention paid for by the SBC charge, not something the company funds in cash. REHABILITATION: restoration and rehabilitation provisions of A$338.8m are deducted in the equity bridge after tax, because cash spent discharging them (A$19.6m in FY2026) runs through operating cash flow against the provision and is not in EBITDA. TAX: the Malaysian pioneer-status tax holiday ended in February 2026; Lynas Malaysia is now a full taxpayer at 24% against 30% in Australia. FY2026 cash tax was a A$7.7m refund and A$42.1m of tax-effected losses are recognised, so the cash tax rate ramps to a blended 27% by year three. FY2027 YEAR-ONE EVIDENCE: the September-quarter FY2027 figures used for the year-one run-rate (average selling price A$102.1/kg, NdPr production 2,082t, floor-price agreements covering more than half of production) come from the qualitative Analysis JSON; that quarterly report is not among the extracted filings and was not independently checked. Management gives no group revenue, earnings or capex guidance.

bear.growth_note: Year one still benefits from the first half already sold at high prices. The market price then falls back to US$55-60/kg, volume stalls near 8,500tpa NdPr, and the floor protects only the ~5,000tpa firm JARE tonnage. Revenue settles around A$1.1-1.2bn.

base.growth_note: Year one (+40%, ~A$1.37bn) is the September-quarter FY2027 run-rate: ~2,080t NdPr a quarter at a realised price near the US$110/kg floor. After that NdPr volume climbs to ~10,000tpa by FY2030 while the market price on the uncovered half fades to a mid-cycle ~US$80/kg, giving a blended ~US$95/kg and revenue of ~A$1.6bn in FY2030. Growth then runs at 2.5-3%.
base.margin_note: FY2026 EBITDA margin was 39.5% with new plants still ramping; FY2021-FY2026 averaged about 42% (range 18% to 65%). 50% in year one reflects the price step and fixed-cost absorption; the path fades to 46% as the uncovered price normalises and costs for the Malaysian residue-process change arrive.
base.capex_note: FY2026 capex was A$178.3m. Years one and two carry the A$294m Lynas Malaysia heavy rare earths expansion, Mt Weld tailings storage, the Isamill and the Kalgoorlie water plant. Long-run capex is set equal to D&A at 10% of revenue.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables rose A$99m and inventories A$52m on A$421m of revenue growth in FY2026. Growth consumes cash.

bull.growth_note: Revenue reaches ~A$2.7bn by FY2031: NdPr at the full 12ktpa, market price held at or above the US$110/kg floor on all volume, and the heavy rare earths suite contributing several hundred million dollars at ex-China prices.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: Lynas sells one product family whose reference price is set by Chinese policy, its Malaysian licence now carries a binding 2031 residue condition that depends on an unproven process, and it has no permanent CEO. Base at 50%: the floor-priced half of the book and the run-rate already visible in the September quarter make the mid-cycle path the most likely. Bull cut from the 35% default to 25%: it needs price, full volume, heavy rare earths pricing and clean execution to all go right together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
